Printf Debugging at 1ns: High-Performance C++ Logging Without Locks - Greg Law - ACCU 2025 Short Talks
---

C++ debugging often starts with printf statements—but what if you could make printf run in just 1ns? In this lightning talk from ACCU 2025, Greg Law (founder of Undo and long-time debugging tool expert) takes you on a journey to reinvent printf debugging for high-performance, multithreaded systems.

Traditional printf debugging is notoriously intrusive and slow, especially in concurrent C++ applications. Lock contention, system call overhead, and thread perturbation all contribute to poor performance and unreliable results. Greg explains why standard logging functions like `fprintf` and `sprintf` fall short, particularly in debugging concurrency issues like race conditions and Heisenbugs.
